caption:
OpenAI president Greg Brockman says most of the company's revenue now comes from businesses, not consumers.
Asked on stage at a Wall Street Journal tech conference if OpenAI will be ready to go public next year, he said: "I think so."
OpenAI is pushing its Codex agent to companies as it competes with Anthropic.

Would you buy OpenAI stock if it went public in 2027?

site_article.headline: Brockman says OpenAI now earns most of its revenue from businesses and could be ready to go public in 2027
site_article.dek: Speaking at a Wall Street Journal conference, OpenAI's president said the company is pushing its Codex agent to enterprise customers as it competes with Anthropic.
site_article.summary: OpenAI president Greg Brockman said on November 4, 2026, that enterprise sales now account for the majority of the company's revenue. Asked whether OpenAI would be ready for an initial public offering next year, he answered that he thought so.
site_article.seo_title: Brockman: OpenAI enterprise sales lead, IPO possible in 2027
site_article.seo_description: OpenAI president Greg Brockman says most revenue now comes from enterprises and that the company could be ready to go public in 2027.
site_article.answer_summary: OpenAI has not set an IPO date, but president Greg Brockman said on November 4, 2026, that he thinks the company will be ready to go public in 2027, and that enterprise sales now bring in most of its revenue.

paragraphs.text: OpenAI now earns the majority of its revenue from enterprise sales, the company's president, Greg Brockman, said on November 4, 2026. He made the remarks on stage at a Wall Street Journal technology conference in Napa, California, according to Reuters.

Asked whether OpenAI would be ready for an initial public offering next year, Brockman replied, "I think so," Reuters reported. The answer signaled confidence about the timing without committing the company to a 2027 listing, Unite.AI noted.

Brockman said OpenAI has been increasing its sales to businesses and is promoting its Codex coding agent as part of that effort, as it competes with Anthropic for corporate customers. Reuters reported that Anthropic is likely to go public before the end of 2026.

The comments mark a change from the mix OpenAI described earlier in the year. In a March 31, 2026, announcement, the company said enterprise accounted for more than 40 percent of its revenue and that it was on track to reach parity with consumer revenue by the end of 2026, according to Unite.AI. At that time, OpenAI said it was generating about $2 billion in revenue per month and that ChatGPT had more than 900 million weekly active users and over 50 million subscribers.

Brockman's session, titled "OpenAI's Race to Scale," was led by Wall Street Journal reporter Keach Hagey and covered AI infrastructure, the evolution of ChatGPT's business, safety and cybersecurity, according to the conference program cited by Unite.AI.

OpenAI has delayed its plans to go public and has instead been racing to raise money to build on its recent growth, Reuters reported. Its most recent funding round closed with $122 billion in committed capital at an $852 billion post-money valuation, with Amazon, NVIDIA and SoftBank anchoring the round and Microsoft continuing to participate, Unite.AI reported, citing the company's March announcement.
The company also expanded its revolving credit facility to about $4.7 billion, which was undrawn when the round closed, according to the same announcement.

OpenAI has described reliable access to computing power as an advantage that compounds across research, products and serving costs. Unite.AI reported that the company's infrastructure now spans several cloud providers, chip platforms and data center partners, after it expanded beyond a small group of core suppliers over roughly the previous 15 months.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the enterprise figure matters as much as the IPO comment. Investors in a public offering would look for steady, contract-based revenue, and a business customer base that now outweighs consumer subscriptions gives OpenAI a story closer to that of a traditional software company. It also invites direct comparison with Anthropic, which Reuters expects to reach the public markets first.

The next signal to watch is whether OpenAI hires banks or files confidential paperwork for a listing, and how the market receives Anthropic's offering, which is likely to set the benchmark for valuing large AI labs.
